title: UART frame (asynchronous serial)
summary: A UART (Universal Asynchronous Receiver/Transmitter) frame: start bit (low), 5-9 data bits (LSB first), optional parity bit, 1-2 stop bits (high). No clock line; baud rate must be agreed upon. Common: 8 data bits, no parity, 1 stop bit (8N1) at 9600/115200 baud.

ext.summary: A UART (Universal Asynchronous Receiver/Transmitter) frame: start bit (low), 5-9 data bits (LSB first), optional parity bit, 1-2 stop bits (high). No clock line; baud rate must be agreed upon. Common: 8 data bits, no parity, 1 stop bit (8N1) at 9600/115200 baud.

structure.meaning: Always 0 (low). Signals the beginning of a frame.
Optional: even/odd/mark/space parity for error detection.
Always 1 (high). Signals the end of a frame.
8 data + no parity + 1 stop = 10 bits per byte. Most common configuration.

ext.example_decoded: UART 8N1 frame for byte 0x00: start(0) + 8 data bits(0) + stop(1)
notes: UART is asynchronous: no shared clock; both sides must agree on baud rate.
UART is used for serial consoles, GPS, Bluetooth modules, and many embedded systems.
RS-232 (voltage levels ±3-15V) and TTL (0-3.3V/5V) are common physical layers.
UART is the simplest and most universal serial interface.
